semantics: Project-created review metadata. Versions include witnesses, components, translations and unresolved leads; their count is not a count of substantive revisions. Acquisition does not establish transcription, collation, normative revision or local reception. No ancestry is asserted.

uses.label: Russian Greek Catholic Church
uses.finding: Roman Russian-use books 1940-1953 remain the candidates; a 1983 Recensio Vulgata Sluzhebnik is proposed as a record, and later reissues (1949, 1962, 1969, 1978) and the parish's 1956 date are labelled leads. Initial use of Russian Synodal books is reported without editions.
uses.limit: No title or approval leaf of any Vulgata book was inspected; parish lists are not dated receipt; Old Rite books unidentified.
next_sources: Title and approval leaves of the 1942, 1953 and 1983 Sluzhebniks (Russicum or Pontifical Oriental Institute libraries)
uses.review_remaining_gap: No title or approval leaf of any Vulgata book inspected; the parish's 'Sluzhebnik 1956' unexplained; Synodal editions used before 1940 unnamed; Russian Catholic receipt of each printing undated.

uses.label: Russian Catholic Old Rite (Old Ritualist community received in 1918)
uses.finding: Community attested by the cold reviewer's source; no book identified.
uses.limit: No search of Old Rite printed books in Catholic use was possible within the bound.
uses.review_remaining_gap: Pre-Nikonian books actually used and their source edition; postulation and exarchate archives.

uses.label: Ruthenian Greek Catholic tradition (Mukachevo, Pittsburgh and daughter jurisdictions)
uses.finding: The 1905 Lviv book was used in Transcarpathia and by Transcarpathian parishes in the United States (Keleher); Mukachevo reprinted the 1941 Chrysostom in 1944; the Mukachevo, Pittsburgh and Philadelphia bishops blessed the 1930 Lviv small Liturgikon after a Rome meeting of October 1929.
uses.limit: Blessing is not proof of use; no Mukachevo-printed original edition was identified; the 1944 reprint is unseen.
next_sources: Acts of the October 1929 Rome meeting
uses.review_remaining_gap: Mukachevo 19th-century books (Buda and Uzhhorod printing) uninspected; the acts of the October 1929 Rome meeting not located; no title leaf of the 1940/1942 originals; 1944 reprint unseen.

uses.label: Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church
uses.finding: Galician line documented from the Lviv Stauropegion 1712 variants through Univ 1733-1747, Pochaiv 1734-1809 (1788 acquired), Lviv 1780, Przemyśl 1840, Lviv 1850 and 1866, the 1899 and 1927 extracts, 1905, 1929 Part I and the 1930 small Liturgikon; the commission names Rome 1942 and Archieratikon 1973 as official.
uses.limit: Most 18th- and 19th-century editions known only from repertoires; the long 19th-century stretch is cited, not inspected.
next_sources: Univ 1740 issues with and without the added propers
uses.review_remaining_gap: Most 18th- and 19th-century editions are known only from repertoires; parent edition of the pre-1894 fragment; Lviv 1929 Part II; Pochaiv Diakonikon 1764 and 1788 not labelled.

uses.label: Belarusian Greek Catholic Church
uses.finding: The historical Uniate printing chain in Belarusian lands is now labelled: Vilnius 1617 Mamonych, Vilnius 1691 small book, 1692-1695, Supraśl 1716 pontifical, 1727-1732, 1758, undated 1750s-1760s excerpts, 1763 and Vilnius 1773.
uses.limit: Only 1617 and 1758 were inspected; 1796-1839 printing and the modern Church's books are unresearched beyond a reported 2004 translation.
next_sources: Belarusian Greek Catholic exarchate liturgical publications
uses.review_remaining_gap: Uniate printing 1796-1839 in the Russian Empire; the 20th-century Belarusian Greek Catholic exarchate's books; the modern Church's books beyond a reported 2004 translation. The Belarusian mapping of metropolia books follows the 1692-1695 baseline convention and is not evidence about the modern Church.

uses.label: Slovak Greek Catholic Church
uses.finding: Roman Ruthenian books are binding in the Košice eparchy; the 1952 Liturgikon cited as a Slovak source is a photolithographic reissue of 1942 (Kolupaev), so the 1940 Chrysostom and 1942 Liturgikon are proposed as Slovak candidates; Prešov's administrator blessed the 1930 Lviv small Liturgikon.
uses.limit: Dated local implementation records and pre-1940 Slovak-owned books remain unseen.
next_sources: Prešov archeparchy archive circulars implementing the Roman books
Lacko's bibliography of Slovak books abroad 1945-1965
uses.review_remaining_gap: Dated Prešov implementation circulars; pre-1905 books used in the Prešov eparchy; Lacko's bibliography of Slovak books abroad.

versions.label: Книга Служебникъ, в нейже блаженых трехъ епископовъ литургіе съвершаються ... (Vilnius: Leon Mamonych, 1617)
versions.tradition_or_use: Kyivan Uniate metropolia; first Sluzhebnik printed specifically for Catholic Ruthenians (Huculak); later Church mapping requires reception evidence
versions.date_label: 1617 (title, Cyrillic numerals); dedication to Lev Sapieha dated Vilnius 1 January 1617 (Kniga Belarusi)
versions.distinctness_basis: Catalogue and repertoire contents: a Nauka (instruction) for priests absent from the Brotherhood edition of 1617 (Huculak, App. II; Kniga Belarusi nos. 80-81).
versions.unresolved: Leaf-by-leaf collation and textual comparison with the 1617 Brotherhood edition.

versions.label: Литургиа иже во святых отца нашего Иоанна Златоустаго ... (Vilnius: Holy Trinity monastery, 1691)
versions.tradition_or_use: Basilian Holy Trinity monastery, Vilnius; small Chrysostom Liturgikon for private celebration; Church mapping requires reception evidence
versions.distinctness_basis: Kniga Belarusi no. 167: a small folio book for priests celebrating privately without singing and while travelling, issued because the full Sluzhebnik (completed at Supraśl in 1695) could not be finished quickly; it reuses leaves prepared for that full book and includes services for St Josaphat and the departed. The same purpose statement recurs in Supraśl 1758.
versions.unresolved: Copy not inspected; relation to 1692-1695 leaves from catalogue only.

versions.label: Понтификал си ест Служебник святительский ... (Supraśl, 1716)
versions.tradition_or_use: Kyivan Uniate metropolia; first Catholic Ruthenian printed pontifical (Huculak)
versions.distinctness_basis: Kniga Belarusi no. 201: hierarchical Liturgy (ff. 1-15), ordinations, consecration of antimensia and chrism, with musical notation. Prepared under Metropolitan Lev Kyshka (Huculak). Zabolotna (2024) reports that the Univ bishop's Sluzhebnik of 1740 partly reproduces it.
versions.unresolved: Hierarchical Liturgy text uninspected.

versions.label: Леитоургикон си ест Служебник ... (Supraśl, title 1727; completed 14 January 1732)
versions.tradition_or_use: Kyivan Uniate metropolia after the Synod of Zamość; Belarusian lands per Senchenko; wider reception unestablished
versions.date_label: Title 1727; colophon p. 478 records printing begun 1727 under Metropolitan Lev Kyshka and finished 14 January 1732 under Metropolitan Atanasii Sheptytsky
versions.distinctness_basis: Senchenko pp. 43-45 reports Josaphat commemoration, Filioque and papal commemoration in this text; Huculak places it in the Zochowski line after Zamość.
versions.unresolved: Copy uninspected; contents reported differently by Kniga Belarusi and Senchenko.

versions.label: Служебник (Univ, 1740)
versions.tradition_or_use: Univ Basilian press under Metropolitan Atanasii Sheptytsky; Galician Uniate use; reception unquantified
versions.distinctness_basis: Huculak: second Univ Sluzhebnik, 2°, [5] + 473 pp., following the Zochowski tradition and the preceding Univ style. Zabolotna: not a textual reproduction of 1733, and part of the print run adds services for St Anthony of Padua and St Casimir absent from other Univ Sluzhebniks. Shmanko (cited by the cold reviewer, not opened here) calls it a repeat of 1733; the disagreement stays open.
versions.unresolved: Conflicting secondary accounts (not a reproduction of 1733 vs a repeat of 1733); copy uninspected.

versions.label: Служебник святительский (Univ, 1740)
versions.tradition_or_use: Univ press; bishop's book; reception unquantified
versions.distinctness_basis: Huculak: printed under Metropolitan Atanasii Sheptytsky, 2°, [3] + 300 pp. Zabolotna: partly reproduces the Supraśl Pontifical of 1716, including an identical Greek chant with notation and the admonition on the chrism ingredients.
versions.unresolved: Copy uninspected.

versions.label: Служебник (Univ, 1747)
versions.tradition_or_use: Univ press; Galician Uniate use; reception unquantified
versions.distinctness_basis: Huculak: third Univ edition, 2°, [4] + 293 folios, Zochowski and Univ tradition. Zabolotna (2024) says it is not a textual reproduction of 1733. NBUV copies Кир.5645п, 5646п and 1268 have Pochaiv [1765] Chrysostom issues inserted in place of removed original leaves (Zabolotna 2015).
versions.unresolved: Nature of difference from 1733 unspecified.

versions.label: Возслідованіе праздником (Univ, 1738 and 1745)
versions.tradition_or_use: Univ press; supplements to existing Sluzhebniks; reception unquantified
versions.distinctness_basis: Zabolotna (2024): services first published at Supraśl for the Catholic feasts of the Holy Eucharist and the Compassion of the Mother of God and for St Josaphat, printed to supplement existing Sluzhebniks and bring them into line with confessional changes. A 1738 copy survives bound in NBUV composite Кир.495 and Кир.950 (Zabolotna 2015).
versions.unresolved: Texts uninspected; two printings not compared.

versions.label: Вослѣдованія праздником пресвятой тайни євхаристіи (Pochaiv, 1741, 1742, 1757, 1762)
versions.tradition_or_use: Pochaiv Basilian press; supplements for the feast of the Eucharist; reception unquantified
versions.distinctness_basis: Zhelezniak pp. 357-358 lists four printings, all held by NBUV; Zabolotna (2015) records the 1741 and 1742 printings bound with older Lviv and Chernihiv office books. Proper texts for a Latin-origin feast supplied apart from the Sluzhebnik.
versions.unresolved: Texts uninspected.

versions.label: Служебник / Літургіаріон (Pochaiv, 1734, 1735, 1744, 1755, 1765, 1778, 1791, 1809) and separate Chrysostom issues (1765, 1778, 1791, 1793)
versions.tradition_or_use: Pochaiv Basilian press (Uniate 1713-1831); priests' Sluzhebnik printings other than 1788
versions.date_label: Printings reported 1734-1809; 1734 an excerpt of 1735 (Huculak); 1744 doubtful (Huculak) but listed and held by NBUV (Zhelezniak)
versions.distinctness_basis: Zhelezniak: nine Sluzhebnik printings (1734, 1735, 1744, 1755, 1765, 1778, 1788, 1791, 1809) and five Chrysostom printings; NBUV holds eight Sluzhebnik printings. Huculak: 1755 prints read (low) Liturgy rubrics at the end; 1765 has a separate Chrysostom excerpt; 1780 and 1785 doubtful. NBUV composites show Pochaiv [1765] Chrysostom issues A, F and G inserted into older books. The 1788 printing is
versions.unresolved: Unexamined range: every Pochaiv printing 1734-1809 except 1788; differences in rubrics (for example low-Liturgy rubrics in 1755) need copy comparison.

versions.label: Леітоургіаріон или Служебникъ, содержащъ въ себѣ по чину Святыя Восточныя Церкве Літургіи ... Четвертое тупомъ изадеся. Въ Обители Почаевской. Року Божія 1788
versions.tradition_or_use: Pochaiv Basilian press; Uniate Volhynian and wider use unquantified; the scanned copy carries parish manuscript entries of unknown place
versions.date_label: 1788 (title, Cyrillic numerals; the commission's link label 1798 is wrong)
versions.distinctness_basis: Title, preface ('Mirror for priests') and opening Proskomedia inspected; contents at the end. Huculak: 2°, [3] + 114 folios + 14 + [2]; follows the Zochowski tradition with some rubrics similar to the Roman Greek Euchologion of 1754. NBUV holds a copy (Кир.3235п). A Lviv bookseller's stamp and later manuscript name lists appear in the scanned copy.
versions.unresolved: Leaf completeness and the reported Benedictine-euchology rubrics not checked.

versions.label: Служебник в нем же литургиа иже во святых отца нашего Иоанна Златоустаго ... в удобнейшее употребление иереем, изрядне еже наедине без пения литургисающим и в путешествиях сущим (Supraśl, 1758)
versions.tradition_or_use: Supraśl Basilian monastery; Uniate metropolia in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth; reception unquantified
versions.distinctness_basis: Inspected contents show Latin-origin feasts and saints in the propers of a Chrysostom book for private (read) celebration; continuity with the 1691 Vilnius small book is catalogue-based.
versions.unresolved: Liturgy text not compared with 1691 or 1692-1695.

versions.label: Леитоургиарион си есть Служебник ... Вторицею типом издадеся в общежителном монастыре Супраслском ... 1763
versions.tradition_or_use: Supraśl Basilian monastery; full Liturgiarion; reception unquantified
versions.distinctness_basis: RSL and Kniga Belarusi no. 239: 2°, 9 unnumbered leaves, pp. 1-196, 1-508, 1-112 = 834 pp., with menaion, common services and services for patrons of Poland and Lithuania (John Nepomucene, Francis, Ignatius Loyola, Casimir). Huculak: Zochowski tradition but without the low (read) Liturgy rubrics. The RSL PDF requires an account sign-in and was not acquired.
versions.unresolved: Book images behind RSL login; copy uninspected.

versions.label: Служебник в нем же литургиа святаго Иоанна Златоустаго со службою на всяк день за упокой содержится (Supraśl, undated)
versions.tradition_or_use: Supraśl press; small Chrysostom books; reception unquantified
versions.date_label: Undated; 1750s-1760s attributed by Labyntsev (Kniga Belarusi nos. 248-250)
versions.distinctness_basis: Kniga Belarusi nos. 249 and 250 (RSL nos. 7533 and 7534): Proskomedia, Chrysostom Liturgy, note on lay communion and a daily requiem service, paginated as excerpts (pp. 189-196 and 1-28); no. 248 is a further undated Supraśl Sluzhebnik described from a defective copy. Excerpt pagination matches the 1763 book's Proskomedia pages, suggesting offprints; not verified.
versions.unresolved: Unexamined range: RSL copies nos. 7533 and 7534 and the defective copy of no. 248; whether they are offprints of 1763.

versions.label: Служебник содержащ в себе литургию иже во святих отца нашего Иоанна Златоустаго ... таже службе две ... (Vilnius, 1773)
versions.tradition_or_use: Basilian Holy Trinity monastery, Vilnius, with Metropolitan Felicjan Filip Wołodkowicz's blessing
versions.distinctness_basis: Kniga Belarusi no. 255: 2°, 3 unnumbered leaves, pp. 1-38; Proskomedia, Chrysostom, services for the departed and the Holy Trinity. Huculak lists it as the Wołodkowicz edition.
versions.unresolved: Copy uninspected.

versions.label: Служебник (Lviv: Stauropegion, 1712), two variants
versions.tradition_or_use: Lviv Stauropegion Brotherhood after its union (1708); Mohylan text used by Catholics
versions.date_label: 1712 printing; corrected variant after Atanasii Sheptytsky's letter of 4 May 1738
versions.distinctness_basis: Reported rubric correction at the Proskomedia in one variant (Huculak).
versions.unresolved: Corrected variant's printing date and extent of changes.

versions.label: Служебник (Lviv, 1780)
versions.tradition_or_use: Lviv; approved by Metropolitan Lev Sheptytsky (Huculak)
versions.distinctness_basis: Huculak: 2°, [3] + 147 + 177 folios, approved by Metropolitan Lev Sheptytsky. Keleher lists Lviv 1780 among books modelled on Zochowski. A copy is reported in Tarkovič's library at Prešov (cold reviewer source, not opened here), which is ownership, not use.
versions.unresolved: Copy uninspected; approval text unseen.

versions.label: Служебник (Przemyśl, 1840)
versions.tradition_or_use: Przemyśl Greek Catholic eparchy; nineteenth-century Galician use
versions.distinctness_basis: Huculak cites its Chrysostom rubrics by page (for example CHR pp. 21, 28, 33, 36, 45) beside 1850 Lviv and 1866 Lviv; Keleher lists 1840 Peremyshl. A defective copy is reported at Prešov (cold reviewer source). The 1866 Lviv page references coincide with 1840, suggesting a reprint; unverified.
versions.unresolved: Copy uninspected; reprint relation to 1866 unverified.

versions.label: Служебник (Lviv, 1850)
versions.tradition_or_use: Lviv Greek Catholic archeparchy; nineteenth-century use
versions.distinctness_basis: Huculak cites its Chrysostom rubrics by folio (for example f. 10r, 12v, 14v, 18r) beside 1840 Przemyśl and 1866 Lviv.
versions.unresolved: Copy uninspected.

versions.label: Служебник (Lviv, 1866)
versions.tradition_or_use: Lviv Greek Catholic archeparchy; nineteenth-century use
versions.distinctness_basis: Huculak cites it with the same Chrysostom page numbers as 1840 Przemyśl; Keleher lists L'viv 1866 in the Zochowski line.
versions.unresolved: Copy uninspected; possibly a reprint of 1840.

versions.label: Чинъ Божественныя Літургіи: Проскомидія Літургіямъ (printed pp. 299 ff.) with occasional and requiem services (pp. c. 605-662), fragment
versions.tradition_or_use: Unidentified Galician printed Sluzhebnik; the fragment was removed at a parish rebinding in 1894
versions.date_label: Printing date unknown; manuscript rebinding note dated 1894
versions.distinctness_basis: Linked by the commission as 'Lviv 1894?'. The manuscript note on printed p. 299 says that when the Sluzhebnik was rebound in 1894 a new Chrysostom Liturgy and services were supplied free of charge and the old ones taken out and bound here, signed by a parish priest. This matches the replacement practice documented for older books (Zabolotna 2015). The commemoration of a metropolitan at p. 315 sugg
versions.unresolved: Parent edition unidentified; compare pagination with Lviv 1866 and other 19th-century full Sluzhebniks.

versions.label: Божественная Літургія иже во святыхъ отца нашего Іоанна Златоустаго ... съ службами недѣлными, дневными, общими святымъ, такожде на всякое прошеніе и о усопшихъ (Zhovkva, 1927)
versions.tradition_or_use: Przemyśl Greek Catholic eparchy permission; Basilian press at Zhovkva; use beyond the eparchy unquantified
versions.date_label: 1927 (title, Cyrillic numerals); printing permission Przemyśl, 5 March 1927, no. 797
versions.distinctness_basis: The commission links it as a small Sluzhebnyk of Przemyśl 1927; the title page gives Zhovkva and the Basilian press, and the verso carries the Przemyśl Greek Catholic Ordinariate's permission signed by auxiliary Bishop Hryhorii (Lakota). Chrysostom Liturgy with Sunday, daily, common, votive and requiem services; text ends at printed p. 160. Comparable in type to the 1842 and 1899 Lviv extracts.
versions.unresolved: Text not compared with 1899 or 1930 extracts.

versions.label: Meeting of Ruthenian-tradition bishops in Rome, October 1929, which settled the order and rules of the Liturgy (as stated in the 1930 Mikron Leitourgikon)
versions.tradition_or_use: Bishops of Lviv, Stanislaviv, Przemyśl, Križevci, Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, Mukachevo, Prešov (administrator) and Canada, with Lviv and Przemyśl auxiliaries
versions.distinctness_basis: The 1930 Lviv small Liturgikon is issued with the blessing of eleven named bishops 'who assembled at the meeting held in the city of Rome in October 1929' and 'established and confirmed the order and rules of the holy Liturgy' (PDF images 2-4). The acts of the meeting and their relation to the Roman commission that produced the 1940-1942 books were not located.
versions.unresolved: Acts of the meeting not located.

versions.label: МІКРОН ЛЕІТОУРГІКОН сиречь Малый Служебникъ, содержай по чину Святыя Кадолическія Восточныя Церкве Літургію ... Іоанна Златоустаго (Lviv, 1930)
versions.tradition_or_use: Lviv archeparchy publication blessed by bishops of several Ruthenian-tradition jurisdictions; use in each jurisdiction unestablished
versions.distinctness_basis: Chrysostom Liturgy with Proskomedia and services for various intentions and common saints, published at the expense of the Lviv archeparchy fund and printed by the Stauropegion Institute. Text corrected after old Slavonic and Greek books by Fr Spyridon Karkhut. Front matter names the blessing of Sheptytsky (Lviv), Khomyshyn (Stanislaviv), Njaradi (Križevci), Kotsylovsky (Przemyśl), Takach (Pittsbu
versions.unresolved: Text not compared with Lviv 1929 Part I or later Roman books; use in each blessing jurisdiction unestablished.

versions.label: Архиератикон, или Служебник святительский (Rome: Grottaferrata monastery press; title 1973, cover 1975)
versions.tradition_or_use: Roman Slavonic series; compiled after the Ruthenian model for Churches following it (Kolupaev); UGCC official book (commission list)
versions.date_label: Title and verso 1973; cover 1975 (Kolupaev); Košice eparchy history gives 1975
versions.distinctness_basis: Kolupaev: hierarchical book containing the texts for the Liturgy, compiled from variants of the sui iuris Churches that follow the Ruthenian model; cover dated 1975, title and verso 1973. The UGCC commission lists Church Slavonic Archieratikon Rome 1973 as official; the Košice eparchy calls the Archieratikon (1975) the last book of the binding Roman series; a Russian Catholic parish library holds
versions.unresolved: Book uninspected.

versions.label: Служебник (Recensione Volgata) (Rome: Grottaferrata monastery press, 1983)
versions.tradition_or_use: Roman Russian-use (Recensio Vulgata) book for Russian Byzantine-rite Catholics abroad; local use unestablished
versions.distinctness_basis: Kolupaev pp. 390-391: contents Vespers, Compline, Midnight Office, Matins, Liturgy, various orders, menologion, prokeimena and appendices; differs from contemporary Moscow Patriarchate Sluzhebniks by lacking the Izvestie uchitelnoe and naming the feast of All Saints of the Russian land 'в земле русстей'. The parish library catalogue identifies the 1983 book explicitly as Recensione Volgata.
versions.unresolved: Book uninspected; relation to 1942 and 1953 unresolved.
